newsitem.title: USA: Clinton backs gay anti-discrimination bill.
newsitem.headline: Clinton backs gay anti-discrimination bill.

text.p: President Clinton Thursday urged Congress to pass a bill that would make it unlawful for an employer to fire gays or lesbians because of their sexual orientation.

The bill is "about the right of each individual in America to be judged on their merits and abilities and to be allowed to contribute to society without facing unfair discrimination," he said in a statement.

Saying it currently is legal in 41 states to fire someone because of his or her sexual preference, Clinton said the legislation was part of "our ongoing fight against bigotry and intolerance, in our country and in our hearts."
Clinton met at the White House with the some of the bill's chief congressional sponsors, including Sen. Edward Kennedy and Representative Barney Frank, both Massachusetts Democrats.
